title: Sweet Potato, Spinach and Quinoa Burgers with Feta
changes_from_base: Baked sweet potato mashed with spinach, quinoa and red lentils makes a soft, colourful patty with a Mediterranean lean from feta, mint and chives; the patties are rolled in panko, chilled and pan-fried.
summary: Vibrant and creamy, these patties combine roasted sweet potato with fresh herbs, tangy cheese and wholesome grains.
equipment: wire rack set in a baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
panko breadcrumbs or chickpea flour, for coating (you will not need it all)
plain yoghurt mixed with a little grated garlic and mint, to serve

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Place 680 g scrubbed sweet potatoes in the oven at 200 °C for 45-60 min until very soft, then remove and cool completely.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Simmer 60 g rinsed quinoa and 65 g rinsed red lentils with 400 ml water and ½ tsp salt covered over medium heat for 15-20 min until tender.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Drain the cooked grains, return to the pan, lay a clean tea towel over the top, put the lid on and leave for 15 min to steam and dry out completely.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Peel and mash the cooled sweet potatoes, stir in 90 g chopped fresh spinach, then fold in the dried grains, 85 g crumbled feta, 3 tbsp chopped fresh mint, 4 tbsp finely chopped chives, 2 tsp lemon juice and ½ tsp ground black pepper.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Shape 10 balls with wet hands, roll in 60 g panko breadcrumbs or chickpea flour and flatten into patties.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Place the patties uncovered on a tray and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over high, swirl to coat the base, drop to medium and fry 5 patties for about 4 min per side until well browned; transfer to a wire rack and repeat with the remaining 2 tbsp oil and patties.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top each patty in a burger bun with a spoonful of yoghurt mixed with grated garlic and fresh mint.

tips: Bake the sweet potatoes until they yield easily to a fork so they mash smoothly
Wet your hands before shaping to prevent the soft mixture sticking
Chill the patties thoroughly so they hold their shape during frying
storage: Shaped patties keep chilled for 2 days; cooked patties keep for 2-3 days or can be frozen, thawed fully and reheated in a low oven for 10-15 min until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
